topic.symptom: Pressing the case power button does nothing at all.
topic.title: Power Button Does Nothing? Check the Front-Panel Pins

script: Power button does nothing? Unplug it before opening the case. Find the front-panel pins in your manual. If the button's plug is on the wrong pins, move it to PWR SW and push it fully on. Plug it back in. Then try the button again.

storyboard.title: Power Button Does Nothing? Check the Front-Panel Pins
storyboard.narrationStyle: Calm, conversational, one check. The captions are burned into the cut; no voice generated.

beats.visualDirection: A finger presses the stylized PC's power button and rests there; nothing lights and the monitor stays dark.

beats.narration: Unplug it before opening the case.
beats.visualDirection: At the back of the power supply, the power cord comes out of the inlet.

beats.narration: Find the front-panel pins in your manual.
beats.visualDirection: A front-panel header from above, labelled EXAMPLE LAYOUT: PWR LED, PWR SW, HDD LED, RESET SW pairs; the POWER SW plug sits on RESET SW; the PWR SW pair glows amber.

beats.narration: If the button's plug is on the wrong pins,
beats.visualDirection: The camera closes in; a red cross beside the plug on RESET SW; the plug lifts and moves to the PWR SW pair.

beats.narration: move it to PWR SW and push it fully on.
beats.visualDirection: The plug is pressed fully onto the PWR SW pins; outlined green.
At the back, the power cord goes back into the power supply.
The unlit PC beside the dark monitor, its button pulsing amber. No one presses it; no start is shown.

factualGuardrails: Never say: guaranteed cure for boot failures (It may not work; one check, never a guaranteed fix.)
Never say: identical pin order across all motherboards (Layouts differ; the cut labels its header EXAMPLE LAYOUT and sends viewers to their manual.)
Never say: successfully boots straight into Windows afterwards (The cut ends before anyone presses the button; no boot is shown or promised.)
persistentDisclosures: Stylized example · not a fix for every PC

claims.proposition: unplug the power cable before working inside the PC

claims.proposition: a case power-switch plug on the wrong front-panel pins can stop the PC powering on
claims.basis: Corsair, "PC Won't Turn On: What You Need to Try" (https://www.corsair.com/us/en/explorer/diy-builder/blogs/pc-wont-turn-on-what-you-need-to-try/): "In some cases, the Power Switch is plugged into the wrong front I/O terminal on the motherboard, preventing the PC from powering on." Checked 2026-10-12 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.

claims.proposition: the motherboard manual shows the front-panel layout, and the button's plug belongs on the PWR SW pins
claims.basis: Corsair, "PC Won't Turn On: What You Need to Try" (https://www.corsair.com/us/en/explorer/diy-builder/blogs/pc-wont-turn-on-what-you-need-to-try/): "Search-excerpt summary: check the motherboard manual for the front I/O connectors; the power switch terminals are often labeled "PWR SW" or "PWR"; on pins such as "RESET SW" or "PWR LED" the PC will not power on." Checked 2026-10-12 via search excerpts; the factual-takeaway gate re-reads it.
